PENDING ON THE FILE OF THE LVI A.C.M.M., NRUPATHUNG ROAD,
BANGALORE CITY FOR THE OFFENCES P/U/S 149, 420, 471, 468,
448, 465 OF IPC, AGAINST THE PETITIONERS VIDE ANNEXURE-B AND A RESPECTIVELY.
 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER FIR was lodged by the 2nd respondent alleging that he had purchased a site in Sy.No.22/1 of Valagerahalli, Kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru from the Karnataka Minorities Building Owners Society and the petitioners-accused colluding with the Revenue authorities got the sub-division of the subject land in the name of Sanjeevappa who had already sold the land in the year 1946.

By mutating the name of Sanjeevappa in the revenue records in collusion with the Revenue Officer, the petitioners got executed the sale deed in the name of his brother-in-law in the year 2003 from the grand children of Sanjeevappa.
The Police registered the FIR for the offence punishable under Sections 149, 420, 471, 468, 448, 465 of IPC.
Taking exception to the same, the petitioners-accused are before this Court.
Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the alleged fabrication of the documents and also the name of Sanjeevappa was mutated in the year 2003.
However, the FIR was lodged after more than 15 years from the date of the alleged incident without offering any plausible explanation.

He further submits that the dispute is with regard to the title over the subject property and the allegations made in the FIR clearly discloses that the dispute between the parties is purely civil in nature however given a criminal texture so as to falsely implicate the petitioners-accused and to wreak vengeance.

sentences.text: 2 3 . On the other hand, learned HCGP for the State and the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2 submits that the petitioners-accused by fabricating the documents in collusion with the revenue authorities got mutated the name of Sanjeevappa who had already sold the subject land way back in the year 1946 and the allegations made in the FIR discloses the commission of cognizable offences and the same requires to be investigated by the Police and at this stage, the registration of the FIR cannot be interfered with and sought for dismissal of the petition.
I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties.

5. Perusal of the FIR lodged by the 2nd respondent discloses that in collusion with revenue authorities, the petitioners-accused got mutated the name of the deceased Sanjeevappa in the revenue records by virtue of the said mutation entries a sale deed was registered in favour of brother-in-law of the petitioners-accused.
The allegation in the FIR is that the Karnataka Minorities Building Owner's Society had formed the layout in the subject land.
The sites formed in the said land was allotted and sold in favour of the 2nd respondent.

6. It is further alleged that due to the torture and mental harassment meted out by the petitioners-accused, one of the site owner Venkatesh committed suicide in the year 2010 and it is suspected that the Venkatesh has not committed suicide but was murdered by the petitioners-accused.
7. The alleged fabrication of the documents and also the revenue entries in favour of Sanjeevappa had taken place in the year 2003.

However, the FIR was lodged on 14.12.2018 NC:
2023:KHC:40985 without offering any plausible explanation.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of State of Andhra Pradesh -vs- M.Madhusudhan Rao, reported in (2008) 15 SCC 582 at para 30 has held as follows:
''30.

entities.text: State of Andhra Pradesh -vs- M.Madhusudhan Rao, reported in (2008) 15 SCC 582
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Time and again, the object and importance of prompt lodging of the first information report has been highlighted.
Delay in lodging the first information report, more often than not, results in embellishment and exaggeration, which is a creature of an afterthought.

A delayed report not only gets bereft of the advantage of spontaneity, the danger of the introduction of a coloured version, an exaggerated account of the incident or a concocted story as a result of deliberations and consultations, also creeps in, casting a serious doubt on its veracity.

Therefore, it is essential that the delay in lodging the report should be satisfactorily explained.''
8.

The allegations made in the FIR clearly discloses that the dispute is with regard to the title over the site formed in Sy. No.22/1 which is alleged to have been purchased by the brother-in-law of the petitioners-accused, which clearly implies that the dispute between the parties is with regard to the title over the said land.
Even otherwise, the FIR was lodged after an NC: 2023:KHC:40985 in-ordinate delay of 15 years from the date of the alleged incident without giving any plausible explanation for the delay.

The Apex Court in the case of Vijay Kumar Ghai & Ors -Vs- The State of West Bengal and Ors.,
reported in at para 21 held as follows:
21.

entities.text: Vijay Kumar Ghai & Ors -Vs- The State of West Bengal and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court has time and again cautioned about converting purely civil disputes into criminal cases.
This Court in Indian Oil Corporation (Supra) noticed the prevalent impression that civil law remedies are time consuming and do not adequately protect the interests of lenders/creditors.

The Court further observed that:-
"13. XXXX any effort to settle civil disputes and claims, which do not involve any criminal offence, by applying pressure through criminal prosecution should be deprecated and discouraged."
10.
Hence, the respondent No.2 instead of availing civil remedy has lodged the FIR to pressurize the petitioners- accused to arrive at a settlement.
11. In view of the preceding analysis, I am of the considered view that the FIR was lodged with an ulterior motive for wreaking vengeance against the petitioners-accused.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) The Criminal Petition is allowed ii) The impugned FIR in Crime No.451/2018 registered by the Kengeri Police Station in so far it relates to accused No.1 is hereby quashed.
iii) It is made clear that this order will not come in the way of respondent No.2 in agitating his rights before the jurisdictional Civil Court.
In view of the disposal of the petition, I.A.No.1/2020 does not survive for consideration and is accordingly disposed of.
